title: Runners are not autodetecting correctly Key error seems to be with muse code but I suspect on others. Muse has just released a new model in the harness however for some reason it is not selectable in the ui ( but is in muse code)  Crutially this hasnt made it sway to the alias choices either, especailly since muse code keeps having its model for aliases wiped.   Please fix all this behaviour and make sure we have a firm and trusted way to build our model catalogue from the attached harnesses. For context the model catalogue should get model options from the runner, convert them into the kainbain standard harness::model::effort and save them then the Ui should allow selecting from that central list.

body:
# Runners are not autodetecting correctly

Key error seems to be with muse code but I suspect on others. Muse has just released a new model in the harness however for some reason it is not selectable in the ui ( but is in muse code) 

Crutially this hasnt made it sway to the alias choices either, especailly since muse code keeps having its model for aliases wiped.  

Please fix all this behaviour and make sure we have a firm and trusted way to build our model catalogue from the attached harnesses. For context the model catalogue should get model options from the runner, convert them into the kainbain standard harness::model::effort and save them then the Ui should allow selecting from that central list.

1|# server2 auto-detect fix — verification record (2026-11-10)
2|
3|## Root cause of the human-reported failure
4|
5|server2's runner env (`~/.kainbain/runner-server2-alpha.env`) pinned
6|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=muse`, so the daemon's harness list was
7|`['muse']` and the discovery round only ran the muse leg — journal showed
8|`Model discovery: 0 model(s) (muse:0)` on every Re-detect, even with the
9|latest runner code deployed. On top of that, the Runner's harness
10|auto-detect probed only PATH, and server2's systemd PATH
11|(`/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`) does not include
12|`~/.local/bin` or `~/.pi/agent/bin`, so even `auto` would have missed pi
13|(the backend's own `discoverHarnesses` detects pi via the
14|`~/.pi/agent/models.json` snapshot, not PATH).
15|
16|## Fix
17|
18|- `runner/daemon.js` `detectAvailableHarnesses` now probes PATH + standard
19|  install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`) + per-harness install dirs
20|  (pi: `~/.pi/agent/bin`, `$PI_AGENT_DIR/bin`) + `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides,
21|  and pi additionally via its `models.json` snapshot — reusing
22|  `standardSearchDirs`/`piSnapshotPath`/`DISCOVERY_ENV_VARS` from
23|  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` so Runner and backend detect the same
24|  harnesses on the same host. `probeHarnessVersions` resolves binaries
25|  through the same dirs (pi now reports a real version, not "unknown").
26|- `startRunner.sh` `detect_harnesses` probes the same set at install time.
27|- server2 ops: env switched to `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=auto` (backup kept
28|  beside it), updated `runner/daemon.js` + `startRunner.sh` copied to the
29|  deployed bundle (md5-verified identical), `systemctl --user restart
30|  kainbain-runner-server2-alpha.service`.
31|
32|## Live verification on server2 (backend http://192.168.1.206:3100)
33|
34|Boot seed (journal, 16:31:33):
35|
36|```
37|Model discovery: 77 model(s) (pi:77, muse:0); next refresh per modelDiscoveryIntervalMs.
38|```
39|
40|`GET /runners` → server2-alpha `status: active`,
41|`capabilities.harnesses: [{id: pi, version: 1.5.0}, {id: muse, version: Muse Code 1.4.15 ...}]`,
42|`capabilities.models`: 77 `pi::…` ids,
43|`capabilities.discoveryStatus: {pi: {ok: true, count: 77, ...}, muse: {ok: true, count: 0, ...}}`.
44|
45|Refresh-button path (the UI "Re-detect models" → `requestModelRediscovery`):
46|
47|```
48|POST /runners/server2-alpha/commands {"command":"requestModelRediscovery"} → 202 queued
49|journal 16:32:48: Runner command: re-detecting models
50|                 Model discovery: 77 model(s) (pi:77, muse:0)
51|GET /runners → commands.results.requestModelRediscovery:
52|  { ok: true, detail: "discovered 77 model(s) (pi:77, muse:0)" }
53|  (rendered by RunnerConfigurationSection as the last re-detection line)
54|```
55|
56|Fleet catalogue: `GET /runners/models/catalogue` → 82 `pi::` entries with
57|`runnerIds: ["server2-alpha"]` — the picker shows them as normal fleet
58|choices with the runner-count badge.
59|
60|Unit tests: `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` 105 pass (incl. 7 new
61|detection cases: standard dirs off PATH, `~/.pi/agent/bin`, pi snapshot,
62|`$PI_AGENT_DIR` snapshot, `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` direct path + bare name,
63|synthetic-mode isolation from the real `~/.pi`); full runner suite
64|300 pass.

meta.output:
Read text file `shared/modelKeys.js`.
1|/***
2| * MARK: modelKeys (shared grammar)
3| * @description THE single implementation of the KainBain model-key grammar,
4| *   shared verbatim by the backend engine (`api/models.js`) and the frontend
5| *   switcher (`frontend/src/services/api.js`) so the two grammars cannot
6| *   drift. Plain ESM, zero dependencies.
7| *
8| *   A model is identified by one of four reference forms:
9| *
10| *     1. `harness::provider::id::reasoning` — CANONICAL with reasoning level (optional 4th segment)
11| *     2. `harness::provider::id`            — CANONICAL, harness-scoped
12| *     3. `provider::id`                     — legacy composite key (still accepted)
13| *     4. bare `id` or `name`                — oldest form (first-match fallback)
14| *
15| *   Parsing rule: split on the FIRST `::`, then the NEXT `::`, then the
16| *   optional THIRD `::` — never `split("::")`, because model ids may contain
17| *   single `:` (e.g. `glm-5.3-flash:cloud`) but never `::`. No segment may
18| *   itself contain `::`; harness ids must be lowercase `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`
19| *   (URL-safe). Malformed keys are rejected (parse returns null, builders throw)
20| *   — they are never parsed incorrectly and passed along silently. Keys with
21| *   5 or more segments are malformed.
22| ***/
23|
24|export const MODEL_KEY_SEP = "::";
25|
26|/** Harness ids are lowercase, start alphanumeric, and are URL-safe. */
27|export const HARNESS_ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$/;
28|
29|/***
30| * MARK: modelKey
31| * @description Builds the legacy provider-scoped composite key for a model so
32| *   the same model id from different providers can be distinguished. Mirrors
33| *   the pi SDK's internal composite identity (`${provider}\0${id}`) but uses
34| *   a printable separator safe for storage and URLs. Still accepted
35| *   everywhere; prefer `harnessModelKey` for new producers.
36| * @example modelKey('ollama-cloud', 'deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud') => 'ollama-cloud::deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud'
37| * @param {string} provider - Provider id (e.g. 'ollama-cloud', 'google').
38| * @param {string} id - Bare model id (may contain single `:`).
39| * @returns {string} Composite `${provider}::${id}` key.
40| ***/
41|export function modelKey(provider, id) {
42|	return `${provider}${MODEL_KEY_SEP}${id}`;
43|}
44|
45|/***
46| * MARK: harnessModelKey
47| * @description Builds the canonical harness-scoped key `harness::provider::id`
48| *   so the same `provider::id` exposed by two different harnesses cannot
49| *   collide. Rejects malformed segments with a thrown error instead of
50| *   building an ambiguous key: the harness id must match
51| *   `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`, and no segment may contain or be empty of the
52| *   `::` separator.
53| * @example harnessModelKey('pi', 'ollama-cloud', 'glm-5.3-flash:cloud') => 'pi::ollama-cloud::glm-5.3-flash:cloud'
54| * @param {string} harness - Harness id (e.g. 'pi').
55| * @param {string} provider - Provider id.
56| * @param {string} id - Bare model id (may contain single `:`).
57| * @returns {string} Canonical `${harness}::${provider}::${id}` key.
58| * @throws {Error} When any segment is empty, contains `::`, or the harness id is not a valid lowercase harness id.
59| ***/
60|export function harnessModelKey(harness, provider, id) {
61|	if (typeof harness !== "string" || !HARNESS_ID_PATTERN.test(harness)) {
62|		throw new Error(
63|			`Invalid harness id '${harness}': must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`,
64|		);
65|	}
66|	if (
67|		typeof provider !== "string" ||
68|		!provider ||
69|		provider.includes(MODEL_KEY_SEP)
70|	) {
71|		throw new Error(
72|			`Invalid model provider '${provider}': must be non-empty and free of '${MODEL_KEY_SEP}'`,
73|		);
74|	}
75|	if (typeof id !== "string" || !id || id.includes(MODEL_KEY_SEP)) {
76|		throw new Error(
77|			`Invalid model id '${id}': must be non-empty and free of '${MODEL_KEY_SEP}'`,
78|		);
79|	}
80|	return `${harness}${MODEL_KEY_SEP}${provider}${MODEL_KEY_SEP}${id}`;

64| *   failing discovery yields `[]`, never the curated fallback — fallback
65| *   models cannot run on that harness, and serving them lets users pick
66| *   models (e.g. pi-flavored entries for antigravity) that can never
67| *   resolve. Only the default harness's flat list keeps the curated fallback
68| *   (offline resilience for the primary picker). A missing or empty registry

77| * @param {boolean} [opts.refresh=false] - Passed through to per-harness listings for non-default entries.
78| * @param {number} [opts.timeoutMs] - Per-harness listing budget (defaults to the configured models timeout).

100|	try {
101|		return await Promise.race([
102|			getAvailableModels({ refresh, harness, fallbackWhenEmpty: false }),
103|			new Promise((resolve) => {
104|				timer = setTimeout(() => resolve([]), timeoutMs);
105|				if (typeof timer.unref === "function") timer.unref();
106|			}),
107|		]);
108|	} finally {
109|		clearTimeout(timer);
110|	}

// Role: full frontend API client — barrel over work/flow/crew/watch/house/retrospective request lists. Base-URL resolution lives in apiBase.js.

import { flowRequests } from './flow/index.js';
import { crewRequests } from './crew/index.js';

/**
 * MARK: api
 * @description Centralized API client for the KainBain frontend.
 * Backward-compatible barrel: implementations live in client/request.js
 * (transport), client/cache.js (TTL caches), modelKeys.js (model grammar),
 * client/docs.js (markdown fetch), and the work/flow/crew/watch/house/
 * retrospective domain lists. This module only composes the `api` object +
 * re-exports.

// Base resolution (loopback self-heal) lives in apiBase.js — one tiny module
// so base-only consumers import it without the whole client, and so the
// `vi.mock('services/api')` test seams stay untouched. The local import feeds
// this module's own wsUrl; the export-from re-exports for every importer.

  API_BASE,
  resolveApiBase,
  isLoopbackHost,
  resolveWsBase,
  pageHostname,
  pageProtocol,
} from './apiBase.js';

export {
  API_BASE,
  resolveApiBase,
  isLoopbackHost,
  resolveWsBase,
} from './apiBase.js';

export {
  DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS,
  MAX_GET_RETRIES,
  request,
} from './client/request.js';

export {
  MODEL_KEY_SEP,
  modelKey,
  harnessModelKey,
  parseModelKey,
  validateModelRefShape,
  splitReasoning,
  stripReasoning,
  appendReasoning,

  classifiesForeignHarness,
  normalizeModelRef,
  resolveModel,
  resolveModelFromRegistry,
  resolveReasoningOptions,

15| *   value are never duplicated. Unknown or malformed ids are skipped.
16| *
17| *   Thin re-export barrel over the one-function-per-file modules in
18| *   `./fleetModelOptions/` — keep this entry point so existing callers
19| *   (model pickers) need no import changes.

{"content":"# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Runner autodetect + trusted model catalogue + alias stability

Task: `9be2458f-c691-4772-90e7-eef1cc2f27c4` — "Runners are not autodetecting correctly".
Stage: plan only. No code changes in this stage.

## 1. Goal

Fix runner autodetect (muse known-broken, others suspected), stop muse alias
targets losing their stored model, and build one firm, trusted model
catalogue: model options flow from each runner's harness discovery into the
kainbain-standard `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` form, are saved
centrally, and the UI selects from that central list.

## 2. Starting evidence (what the codebase shows today)

All paths verified by reading the code this session. No prior report was
taken on trust.

- Runner discovery legs live in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`
  (`DISCOVERY_LEGS`: pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode, codex). Each leg
  reuses its backend harness's own `listModels()` surface, runs behind a
  20s watchdog (`DISCOVER_LEG_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS`), and keeps the previous
  per-harness slice on failure.
- The daemon (`runner/daemon.js`) seeds `discoveredModelsCache` at boot and
  refreshes on `modelDiscoveryIntervalMs` (default 12h,
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js`). Heartbeats advertise
  `models: resolveAdvertisedModels(config, discovered)` — **pin-wins by
  default**: when `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`MODEL` is set,
  `refreshDiscoveredModels` skips scanning entirely unless
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`. A pinned runner can therefore
  never surface a newly released model.
- Runner harness autodetect (`detectAvailableHarnesses`,
  `AUTO_DETECTABLE_HARNESSES = ["pi","muse","antigravity","vibe"]`,
  `HARNESS_DETECT_BINS`, `defaultLoadHarness`) knows only five harnesses.
  **opencode and codex have discovery legs but are absent from runner
  autodetect, version probing, and the runnable-harness loader** — the
  backend resolver (`api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js`) does cover
  codex/opencode (`KAINBAIN_CODEX_BIN`, `KAINBAIN_OPENCODE_BIN`,
  `~/.opencode/bin`). The two sides have drifted.
- Leg asymmetry: codex always throws `CODEX_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` (live
  transport unverified); opencode requires an `OPENCODE_URL` server on the
  runner host (`OPENCODE_NOT_CONFIGURED` otherwise); muse spawns
  `muse serve` stdio `model/list` and throws `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` on a
  zero-row answer.
- The fleet catalogue (`api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.js`,
  `buildFleetModelCatalog`) is derived **live** from claim-eligible runner
  registrations, served at `GET /runners/models/catalogue`, and gated by
  `effectiveRunnerModels` (operator `availableModels` allowlist wins over
  advertised). It is never cached — good — but it is a *second* catalogue,
  not the one the pickers primarily read.
- The pickers primarily read `GET /compute/models` (backend-host catalogue
  via `aggregateModelCatalog` in `api/models.js`, per-harness honest lists,
  curated fallback for the default harness only), fetched once on mount by
  `useModelCatalog` (`frontend/src/hooks/useModelCatalog.js`) with a 60s
  client cache, on top of backend TTLs (shared `modelListCache`, 5-min muse
  MSP cache in `api/agent/harnesses/muse/msp/museMspModelCatalog.js`,
  per-harness timeout in `api/crew/modelDiscovery.js`). Fleet ids are merged
  in client-side by `withFleetModels`/`fleetModelsForHarness`
  (`frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/`) as exact advertised ids with
  strict harness attribution, gated on `fleetLoaded`. So today there are
  **two sources merged in the browser**, with at least four TTLs between a
  new CLI model and a visible option. That explains "new muse model visible
  in muse code but not in the UI".
- "Effort" in the task text does not exist as a catalogue segment. The real
  grammar (`shared/modelKeys.js`) is
  `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]`; runner `tiers` (`T0,T1`,
  `runner/config.js`, dispatch gate `TIER_CEILING`) are a separate fleet
  concept. The plan treats "effort" = reasoning level and keeps tiers
  distinct (see survey assumption q4).
- Alias wipe paths found: (a) `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` harness `onChange`
  always writes `{ harness: next, model: "" }`; (b) `normalizeModelAliases`
  (`shared/modelAliases.js`) **drops** grammar-invalid rows on every
  projectStore write path (`api/projectStore.js`); (c)
  `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` (`api/aliasTargets.js`) blanks models on
  `none`-harness targets at load; (d) save-time hard errors refuse unknown
  harness / `none`+model / malformed ref / unadvertised reasoning level
  (`validateAliasTargetModels`). Catalogue-miss is already soft (warning
  only) — that part matches the desired behaviour and must be preserved.
- Survey state: `SURVEY.md` exists in this task folder but `answers` is
  empty (unanswered), and the referenced `idea-20261110-212333.md` is not
  present in the folder. The plan adopts the survey's Recommended options
  as assumptions (Section 3) and flags them for confirmation.

## 3. Survey assumptions (Recommended options adopted, unconfirmed)

- q1 — scope: **all connected tools, fixed properly** (not muse-only).
- q2 — new-model arrival: **appears on its own at the next automatic
  check** (no manual Refresh required, though Refresh stays as an escape
  hatch).
- q3 — alias target stops being detected: **keep the saved value and show
  a clear warning** (never auto-retarget, never blank, never block saves).
- q4 — "effort" segment: **thinking depth / reasoning level** (the existing
  4th `::reasoning` segment), not speed/quality tier. Tiers stay a separate
  dispatch concept.

If any assumption is wrong, Phase 0 re-plans before code changes.

## 4. Key decisions

1. **Single harness-capability table shared by runner and backend.**
   Autodetect bins, env overrides, version probes, discovery legs, and
   "runnable" status come from one module both sides import, so runner and
   backend can never drift again (fixes the opencode/codex gap
   structurally, not by adding two more entries in one file).
2. **Discovery-wins becomes the safe default; pins become explicit
   allowlists.** Keep pin-wins available as an operator opt-out, but the
   default advertises live discovery (freshness beats upgrade-safety once
   the catalogue is trusted and alias/validation paths never wipe on
   drift). This is the direct fix for "new model never appears".
3. **One central catalogue service on the backend.** It unions
   backend-host listings and per-runner advertised ids, normalises every
   option to canonical `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` via
   `shared/modelKeys.js`, persists the union (so UI and dispatch read the
   same saved list), and records provenance per option (which runner(s) /
   backend host serve it, when last seen). The UI selects from this list;
   the fleet merge moves server-side and the browser stops merging two
   sources.
4. **Aliases never lose data to discovery drift.** Catalogue-miss stays
   soft everywhere; invalid rows are quarantined with a warning instead of
   dropped; harness switches preserve the model text until the user picks a
   replacement.
5. **Muse is the pilot harness, not the only harness.** Every fix lands
   behind the shared table + per-harness contract tests, and the rollout
   proves all six legged harnesses (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode,
   codex-including-its-honest-unavailable state).

## 5. Work plan (research and big pieces first; make-change-easy before the change)

### Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; time-boxed; no behaviour change)

- **0.1 Muse probe parity spike.** Reproduce "new model in muse code, not
  in UI" end to end: run the runner leg (`discoverMuseModels`), the
  backend catalogue probe (`createMuseMspModelCatalog`), and the UI fetch
  chain against a muse CLI serving a model the caches have never seen.
  Measure which layer hides it (pin-wins skip, 12h cadence, 5-min MSP
  cache, `modelListCache` TTL, 60s client cache, `fleetLoaded` gate) and
  record the exact staleness budget. Output: a short findings note +
  failing characterization tests checked in as pending/skipped.
- **0.2 Autodetect matrix spike.** Build the ground-truth matrix
  harness × {runner autodetect, runner version probe, runner runnable
  loader, discovery leg, backend resolver, backend roster,
  UI section} for all eight ids (mock, custom, pi, muse, antigravity,
  vibe, opencode, codex). Confirm opencode/codex gaps and any further
  drift (e.g. codex transport status in `codexHarness.js`, opencode server
  expectations). Output: matrix doc + contract-test skeletons.
- **0.3 Catalogue consolidation design spike.** Decide the persisted
  central catalogue's home (extend the runner registry vs a new store),
  write triggers (heartbeat vs discovery event vs cadence), retention for
  "last seen" provenance, and the exact API shape (extend
  `/runners/models/catalogue`, extend `/compute/models`, or one new
  endpoint). Constraint: dispatch (`runnerMatches.js`,
  `effectiveRunnerModels`) and pickers must read the same saved list.
  Output: ADR-style decision record.

### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (seams, safety nets, no behaviour change)

- **1.1 Extract the shared harness-capability table.** New dependency-free
  module (next to `shared/modelKeys.js`) owning per-harness: autodetect
  bins, env override var, version probe bins, search-dir extras, has-leg,
  runnable-by-default. Rewire runner `daemon.js` tables and
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` to import it. Behaviour identical;
  covered by the Phase 0 matrix tests.
- **1.2 Per-harness discovery contract tests.** For each of the six legs:
  canonical-key output, honest-empty classification, keep-old-slice on
  failure, watchdog timeout, and grammar rejection of malformed rows.
  Codify codex's honest-unavailable and opencode's not-configured as
  specified states, not gaps.
- **1.3 Catalogue provenance plumbing (read-only).** Add last-seen /
  served-by provenance to fleet catalogue entries and surface
  `discoveryStatus` per runner in Settings, without changing selection
  behaviour. This is the observability the later cutover leans on.
- **1.4 Alias safety net.** Characterization tests proving: unknown-model
  saves warn but succeed; reload never drops rows; harness switch keeps
  model text as a visibly-stale value. All red before Phase 3, no prod
  change yet.

### Phase 2 — Fix autodetect (runner + backend agreement)

- **2.1 Bring opencode/codex into the shared table** with correct
  semantics: opencode autodetects via binary *and* reachable-server
  signal (document which counts as "installed" vs "runnable");
  codex autodetects via binary + auth store
  (`codexAuthPath`) while discovery stays honestly unavailable until the
  transport lands.
- **2.2 Single "installed / runnable / discoverable" vocabulary** surfaced
  identically in runner logs, heartbeat `discoveryStatus`, and backend
  harness availability, replacing today's per-side wording.
- **2.3 Stale-pin hint becomes actionable.** `staleHarnessHintFor` already
  detects configured-vs-detected drift; wire it into heartbeat facts and
  Settings so "runner not serving an installed harness" is visible without
  reading logs.

### Phase 3 — Trusted central catalogue (the core change)

- **3.1 Discovery-wins by default.** Flip the default so live discovery
  advertises and pins become explicit allowlists (`availableModels`
  semantics extend to the runner: pin = restrict, not freeze). Keep
  pin-wins as an opt-out flag for frozen fleets. Shorten/refresh cadence
  so q2 ("appears at the next automatic check") holds: keep the 12h tick
  but add discovery on runner (re)connect, on Re-detect command, and a
  bounded staleness cap for the persisted list.
- **3.2 Central catalogue service.** Implement the Phase 0.3 design:
  ingest runner-advertised ids + backend-host listings, normalise to
  canonical keys (reject ungrammatical ids with provenance-logged drops,
  never silent), persist with per-option provenance, serve one endpoint
  the UI and dispatch share. `buildFleetModelCatalog` becomes a view over
  it (or is replaced by it — decided in 0.3).
- **3.3 UI cutover to the central list.** `useModelCatalog` reads the
  central endpoint; `withFleetModels` client-side merging is removed (or
  kept purely as a deprecated fallback for older backends during one
  release); `ModelSelector` and `ModelAliasesSection` render provenance
  ("2 runners · seen 3m ago") instead of today's dual-source badges.
  Refresh bypasses caches end to end (client → central service → legs).
- **3.4 Kill the staleness stack.** Align the four TTLs behind the central
  service: legs cache per-harness slices (keep), central service owns the
  UI-facing TTL, client keeps a short TTL only. A new CLI model must be
  selectable after at most one automatic check + one UI refresh, per q2.

### Phase 4 — Alias stability (keep + warn, per q3)

- **4.1 Never drop on write.** `normalizeModelAliases` quarantines invalid
  rows (kept, flagged, excluded from dispatch) instead of dropping them;
  projectStore surfaces the quarantine in save responses.
- **4.2 Never blank on drift.** `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` load path and
  the `ModelAliasesSection` harness switch preserve model text as a
  visibly-stale value; "Clear" stays an explicit user action.
- **4.3 Unknown harness stays hard, unknown model stays soft** —
  re-verify `validateAliasTargetModels` tiers after the catalogue move so
  a central-catalogue outage can never block alias saves (probe-null ⇒
  warn nothing, as today).

### Phase 5 — Assurance and rollout

- **5.1 Test gates.** `npm run test:unit` green; new suites: shared-table
  parity (runner vs backend resolve identically on fixtures), leg
  contracts, central-catalogue golden tests (ingest → normalise → persist
  → serve), alias no-data-loss tests, UI picker tests against the central
  endpoint (existing `useModelCatalog` / `ModelSelector` /
  `ModelAliasesSection` suites updated, not deleted). Headless checks via
  existing mock fixtures or `npm run capture:screenshot`; no long-lived
  background servers.
- **5.2 Docs.** Update runner docs (autodetect + discovery-wins +
  Re-detect), Settings help text, the model-key grammar doc if "effort"
  wording appears anywhere (rename to reasoning level), and the ADR from
  0.3. Add an operator runbook: "new model not appearing" (check
  discoveryStatus → Re-detect → staleness cap) and "alias target stale"
  (warning meaning + fix path).
- **5.3 Rollout.** Ship Phase 1 behind no flags (refactor only); Phase 2
  with per-harness logging; Phase 3 behind a single
  `centralCatalog` flag with dual-read comparison logging (central vs
  legacy merge) for one release before cutover; Phase 4 with quarantine
  metrics. Rollback = flag off + pin-wins opt-out documented.

## 6. Validation plan (per phase)

- 0.1: reproduction script shows the new-model journey across every layer
  with timestamps; characterization tests fail for the right reason.
- 0.2: matrix has zero "unknown" cells; every cell links to code or a
  contract test.
- 0.3: ADR signed off; dispatch and UI proven to read the same store in a
  spike test.
- 1.1–1.4: `npm run test:unit` green with zero behaviour diff (dual-run
  old vs new tables on fixtures).
- 2.x: fixture-host tests prove opencode/codex detect/no-detect correctly
  on both sides; stale-pin hint visible in heartbeat facts fixture.
- 3.x: golden test — runner advertises `muse::meta::<new>` → central list
  contains it with provenance → picker offers it → dispatch matches it
  verbatim; staleness test — new model selectable within one check cycle.
- 4.x: no-data-loss tests — drifted/invalid/stale alias rows survive
  save → reload → save with warnings and zero silent mutation.
- 5.x: full `npm run test:unit`, lint, docs link check
  (`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` path per repo convention), screenshot
  smoke of picker + aliases pages.

## 7. Risks and open questions

- The survey was never answered; q1–q4 assumptions need owner confirmation
  before Phase 3 (wrong q2/q4 changes the catalogue design).
- Codex live transport is unverified — 2.1 must not promise codex
  discovery, only honest codex detectability.
- Opencode "installed" definition (binary present vs server reachable) is
  genuinely ambiguous — 0.2/2.1 decides, both states stay expressible.
- Behaviour risk: flipping to discovery-wins changes what pinned fleets
  advertise — mitigated by the opt-out flag, dual-read logging, and the
  quarantine path in 4.1.
- Non-goals: new harness additions beyond the eight known ids; changing
  the `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` grammar; dispatch matching
  semantics beyond reading the shared list; UI redesign of the pickers.

## 8. Success criteria

- Every legged harness autodetects identically on runner and backend, with
  contract tests pinning the agreement.
- A model released in any attached harness CLI is selectable in the UI
  after the next automatic check, with no manual Refresh and no alias
  edits.
- Alias targets never lose their stored model to discovery drift; stale
  targets show a clear warning and saves always succeed.
- One persisted central catalogue in canonical form backs the UI pickers,
  alias validation, and dispatch matching.

## 5. Work plan (research and big pieces first; make-change-easy before the change)

### Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; time-boxed; no behaviour change)

- **0.1 Muse probe parity spike.** Reproduce "new model in muse code, not
  in UI" end to end: run the runner leg (`discoverMuseModels`), the
  backend catalogue probe (`createMuseMspModelCatalog`), and the UI fetch
  chain against a muse CLI serving a model the caches have never seen.
  Measure which layer hides it (pin-wins skip, 12h cadence, 5-min MSP
  cache, `modelListCache` TTL, 60s client cache, `fleetLoaded` gate) and
  record the exact staleness budget. Output: a short findings note +
  failing characterization tests checked in as pending/skipped.
- **0.2 Autodetect matrix spike.** Build the ground-truth matrix
  harness × {runner autodetect, runner version probe, runner runnable
  loader, discovery leg, backend resolver, backend roster,
  UI section} for all eight ids (mock, custom, pi, muse, antigravity,
  vibe, opencode, codex). Confirm opencode/codex gaps and any further
  drift (e.g. codex transport status in `codexHarness.js`, opencode server
  expectations). Output: matrix doc + contract-test skeletons.
- **0.3 Catalogue consolidation design spike.** Decide the persisted
  central catalogue's home (extend the runner registry vs a new store),
  write triggers (heartbeat vs discovery event vs cadence), retention for
  "last seen" provenance, and the exact API shape (extend
  `/runners/models/catalogue`, extend `/compute/models`, or one new
  endpoint). Constraint: dispatch (`runnerMatches.js`,
  `effectiveRunnerModels`) and pickers must read the same saved list.
  Output: ADR-style decision record.

### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (seams, safety nets, no behaviour change)

- **1.1 Extract the shared harness-capability table.** New dependency-free
  module (next to `shared/modelKeys.js`) owning per-harness: autodetect
  bins, env override var, version probe bins, search-dir extras, has-leg,
  runnable-by-default. Rewire runner `daemon.js` tables and
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` to import it. Behaviour identical;
  covered by the Phase 0 matrix tests.
- **1.2 Per-harness discovery contract tests.** For each of the six legs:
  canonical-key output, honest-empty classification, keep-old-slice on
  failure, watchdog timeout, and grammar rejection of malformed rows.
  Codify codex's honest-unavailable and opencode's not-configured as
  specified states, not gaps.
- **1.3 Catalogue provenance plumbing (read-only).** Add last-seen /
  served-by provenance to fleet catalogue entries and surface
  `discoveryStatus` per runner in Settings, without changing selection
  behaviour. This is the observability the later cutover leans on.
- **1.4 Alias safety net.** Characterization tests proving: unknown-model
  saves warn but succeed; reload never drops rows; harness switch keeps
  model text as a visibly-stale value. All red before Phase 3, no prod
  change yet.

### Phase 2 — Fix autodetect (runner + backend agreement)

- **2.1 Bring opencode/codex into the shared table** with correct
  semantics: opencode autodetects via binary *and* reachable-server
  signal (document which counts as "installed" vs "runnable");
  codex autodetects via binary + auth store

  transport lands.
- **2.2 Single "installed / runnable / discoverable" vocabulary** surfaced
  identically in runner logs, heartbeat `discoveryStatus`, and backend
  harness availability, replacing today's per-side wording.
- **2.3 Stale-pin hint becomes actionable.** `staleHarnessHintFor` already
  detects configured-vs-detected drift; wire it into heartbeat facts and
  Settings so "runner not serving an installed harness" is visible without
  reading logs.

### Phase 3 — Trusted central catalogue (the core change)

- **3.1 Discovery-wins by default.** Flip the default so live discovery
  advertises and pins become explicit allowlists (`availableModels`
  semantics extend to the runner: pin = restrict, not freeze). Keep
  pin-wins as an opt-out flag for frozen fleets. Shorten/refresh cadence
  so q2 ("appears at the next automatic check") holds: keep the 12h tick
  but add discovery on runner (re)connect, on Re-detect command, and a
  bounded staleness cap for the persisted list.
- **3.2 Central catalogue service.** Implement the Phase 0.3 design:
  ingest runner-advertised ids + backend-host listings, normalise to
  canonical keys (reject ungrammatical ids with provenance-logged drops,
  never silent), persist with per-option provenance, serve one endpoint
  the UI and dispatch share. `buildFleetModelCatalog` becomes a view over
  it (or is replaced by it — decided in 0.3).

  central endpoint; `withFleetModels` client-side merging is removed (or
  kept purely as a deprecated fallback for older backends during one
  release); `ModelSelector` and `ModelAliasesSection` render provenance
  ("2 runners · seen 3m ago") instead of today's dual-source badges.
  Refresh bypasses caches end to end (client → central service → legs).

  service: legs cache per-harness slices (keep), central service owns the
  UI-facing TTL, client keeps a short TTL only. A new CLI model must be
  selectable after at most one automatic check + one UI refresh, per q2.

- **4.1 Never drop on write.** `normalizeModelAliases` quarantines invalid
  rows (kept, flagged, excluded from dispatch) instead of dropping them;
  projectStore surfaces the quarantine in save responses.
- **4.2 Never blank on drift.** `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` load path and
  the `ModelAliasesSection` harness switch preserve model text as a
  visibly-stale value; "Clear" stays an explicit user action.

  re-verify `validateAliasTargetModels` tiers after the catalogue move so
  a central-catalogue outage can never block alias saves (probe-null ⇒

  parity (runner vs backend resolve identically on fixtures), leg
  contracts, central-catalogue golden tests (ingest → normalise → persist
  → serve), alias no-data-loss tests, UI picker tests against the central
  endpoint (existing `useModelCatalog` / `ModelSelector` /
  `ModelAliasesSection` suites updated, not deleted). Headless checks via
  existing mock fixtures or `npm run capture:screenshot`; no long-lived
  background servers.
- **5.2 Docs.** Update runner docs (autodetect + discovery-wins +
  Re-detect), Settings help text, the model-key grammar doc if "effort"
  wording appears anywhere (rename to reasoning level), and the ADR from
  0.3. Add an operator runbook: "new model not appearing" (check
  discoveryStatus → Re-detect → staleness cap) and "alias target stale"
  (warning meaning + fix path).

  with per-harness logging; Phase 3 behind a single
  `centralCatalog` flag with dual-read comparison logging (central vs
  legacy merge) for one release before cutover; Phase 4 with quarantine
  metrics. Rollback = flag off + pin-wins opt-out documented.

## 6. Validation plan (per phase)

- 0.1: reproduction script shows the new-model journey across every layer
  with timestamps; characterization tests fail for the right reason.
- 0.2: matrix has zero "unknown" cells; every cell links to code or a
  contract test.
- 0.3: ADR signed off; dispatch and UI proven to read the same store in a
  spike test.
- 1.1–1.4: `npm run test:unit` green with zero behaviour diff (dual-run
  old vs new tables on fixtures).
- 2.x: fixture-host tests prove opencode/codex detect/no-detect correctly
  on both sides; stale-pin hint visible in heartbeat facts fixture.
- 3.x: golden test — runner advertises `muse::meta::<new>` → central list
  contains it with provenance → picker offers it → dispatch matches it
  verbatim; staleness test — new model selectable within one check cycle.
- 4.x: no-data-loss tests — drifted/invalid/stale alias rows survive
  save → reload → save with warnings and zero silent mutation.
- 5.x: full `npm run test:unit`, lint, docs link check
  (`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` path per repo convention), screenshot
  smoke of picker + aliases pages.

## 7. Risks and open questions

- The survey was never answered; q1–q4 assumptions need owner confirmation
  before Phase 3 (wrong q2/q4 changes the catalogue design).
- Codex live transport is unverified — 2.1 must not promise codex
  discovery, only honest codex detectability.
- Opencode "installed" definition (binary present vs server reachable) is
  genuinely ambiguous — 0.2/2.1 decides, both states stay expressible.
- Behaviour risk: flipping to discovery-wins changes what pinned fleets
  advertise — mitigated by the opt-out flag, dual-read logging, and the
  quarantine path in 4.1.
- Non-goals: new harness additions beyond the eight known ids; changing
  the `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` grammar; dispatch matching
  semantics beyond reading the shared list; UI redesign of the pickers.

## 8. Success criteria

- Every legged harness autodetects identically on runner and backend, with
  contract tests pinning the agreement.
- A model released in any attached harness CLI is selectable in the UI
  after the next automatic check, with no manual Refresh and no alias
  edits.
- Alias targets never lose their stored model to discovery drift; stale
  targets show a clear warning and saves always succeed.
- One persisted central catalogue in canonical form backs the UI pickers,
  alias validation, and dispatch matching.

2|
3|Task: `9be2458f-c691-4772-90e7-eef1cc2f27c4` — "Runners are not autodetecting correctly".
4|Stage: plan only. No code changes in this stage.
5|
6|## 1. Goal
7|
8|Fix runner autodetect (muse known-broken, others suspected), stop muse alias
9|targets losing their stored model, and build one firm, trusted model
10|catalogue: model options flow from each runner's harness discovery into the
11|kainbain-standard `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` form, are saved
12|centrally, and the UI selects from that central list.
13|
14|## 2. Starting evidence (what the codebase shows today)
15|
16|All paths verified by reading the code this session. No prior report was
17|taken on trust.
18|
19|- Runner discovery legs live in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`
20|  (`DISCOVERY_LEGS`: pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode, codex). Each leg
21|  reuses its backend harness's own `listModels()` surface, runs behind a
22|  20s watchdog (`DISCOVER_LEG_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS`), and keeps the previous
23|  per-harness slice on failure.
24|- The daemon (`runner/daemon.js`) seeds `discoveredModelsCache` at boot and
25|  refreshes on `modelDiscoveryIntervalMs` (default 12h,
26|  `runner/modelDiscovery.js`). Heartbeats advertise
27|  `models: resolveAdvertisedModels(config, discovered)` — **pin-wins by
28|  default**: when `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`MODEL` is set,
29|  `refreshDiscoveredModels` skips scanning entirely unless
30|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`. A pinned runner can therefore
31|  never surface a newly released model.
32|- Runner harness autodetect (`detectAvailableHarnesses`,
33|  `AUTO_DETECTABLE_HARNESSES = ["pi","muse","antigravity","vibe"]`,
34|  `HARNESS_DETECT_BINS`, `defaultLoadHarness`) knows only five harnesses.
35|  **opencode and codex have discovery legs but are absent from runner
36|  autodetect, version probing, and the runnable-harness loader** — the
37|  backend resolver (`api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js`) does cover
38|  codex/opencode (`KAINBAIN_CODEX_BIN`, `KAINBAIN_OPENCODE_BIN`,
39|  `~/.opencode/bin`). The two sides have drifted.
40|- Leg asymmetry: codex always throws `CODEX_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` (live
41|  transport unverified); opencode requires an `OPENCODE_URL` server on the
42|  runner host (`OPENCODE_NOT_CONFIGURED` otherwise); muse spawns
43|  `muse serve` stdio `model/list` and throws `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` on a
44|  zero-row answer.
45|- The fleet catalogue (`api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.js`,
46|  `buildFleetModelCatalog`) is derived **live** from claim-eligible runner
47|  registrations, served at `GET /runners/models/catalogue`, and gated by
48|  `effectiveRunnerModels` (operator `availableModels` allowlist wins over
49|  advertised). It is never cached — good — but it is a *second* catalogue,
50|  not the one the pickers primarily read.
51|- The pickers primarily read `GET /compute/models` (backend-host catalogue
52|  via `aggregateModelCatalog` in `api/models.js`, per-harness honest lists,
53|  curated fallback for the default harness only), fetched once on mount by
54|  `useModelCatalog` (`frontend/src/hooks/useModelCatalog.js`) with a 60s
55|  client cache, on top of backend TTLs (shared `modelListCache`, 5-min muse
56|  MSP cache in `api/agent/harnesses/muse/msp/museMspModelCatalog.js`,
57|  per-harness timeout in `api/crew/modelDiscovery.js`). Fleet ids are merged
58|  in client-side by `withFleetModels`/`fleetModelsForHarness`
59|  (`frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/`) as exact advertised ids with
60|  strict harness attribution, gated on `fleetLoaded`. So today there are
61|  **two sources merged in the browser**, with at least four TTLs between a
62|  new CLI model and a visible option. That explains "new muse model visible
63|  in muse code but not in the UI".
64|- "Effort" in the task text does not exist as a catalogue segment. The real
65|  grammar (`shared/modelKeys.js`) is
66|  `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]`; runner `tiers` (`T0,T1`,
67|  `runner/config.js`, dispatch gate `TIER_CEILING`) are a separate fleet
68|  concept. The plan treats "effort" = reasoning level and keeps tiers
69|  distinct (see survey assumption q4).
70|- Alias wipe paths found: (a) `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` harness `onChange`
71|  always writes `{ harness: next, model: "" }`; (b) `normalizeModelAliases`
72|  (`shared/modelAliases.js`) **drops** grammar-invalid rows on every
73|  projectStore write path (`api/projectStore.js`); (c)
74|  `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` (`api/aliasTargets.js`) blanks models on
75|  `none`-harness targets at load; (d) save-time hard errors refuse unknown
76|  harness / `none`+model / malformed ref / unadvertised reasoning level
77|  (`validateAliasTargetModels`). Catalogue-miss is already soft (warning
78|  only) — that part matches the desired behaviour and must be preserved.
79|- Survey state: `SURVEY.md` exists in this task folder but `answers` is
80|  empty (unanswered), and the referenced `idea-20261110-212333.md` is not
81|  present in the folder. The plan adopts the survey's Recommended options
82|  as assumptions (Section 3) and flags them for confirmation.
83|
84|## 3. Survey assumptions (Recommended options adopted, unconfirmed)
85|
86|- q1 — scope: **all connected tools, fixed properly** (not muse-only).
87|- q2 — new-model arrival: **appears on its own at the next automatic
88|  check** (no manual Refresh required, though Refresh stays as an escape
89|  hatch).
90|- q3 — alias target stops being detected: **keep the saved value and show
91|  a clear warning** (never auto-retarget, never blank, never block saves).
92|- q4 — "effort" segment: **thinking depth / reasoning level** (the existing
93|  4th `::reasoning` segment), not speed/quality tier. Tiers stay a separate
94|  dispatch concept.
95|
96|If any assumption is wrong, Phase 0 re-plans before code changes.
97|
98|## 4. Key decisions
99|
100|1. **Single harness-capability table shared by runner and backend.**
101|   Autodetect bins, env overrides, version probes, discovery legs, and
102|   "runnable" status come from one module both sides import, so runner and
103|   backend can never drift again (fixes the opencode/codex gap
104|   structurally, not by adding two more entries in one file).
105|2. **Discovery-wins becomes the safe default; pins become explicit
106|   allowlists.** Keep pin-wins available as an operator opt-out, but the
107|   default advertises live discovery (freshness beats upgrade-safety once
108|   the catalogue is trusted and alias/validation paths never wipe on
109|   drift). This is the direct fix for "new model never appears".
110|3. **One central catalogue service on the backend.** It unions
111|   backend-host listings and per-runner advertised ids, normalises every
112|   option to canonical `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` via
113|   `shared/modelKeys.js`, persists the union (so UI and dispatch read the
114|   same saved list), and records provenance per option (which runner(s) /
115|   backend host serve it, when last seen). The UI selects from this list;
116|   the fleet merge moves server-side and the browser stops merging two
117|   sources.
118|4. **Aliases never lose data to discovery drift.** Catalogue-miss stays
119|   soft everywhere; invalid rows are quarantined with a warning instead of
120|   dropped; harness switches preserve the model text until the user picks a
121|   replacement.
122|5. **Muse is the pilot harness, not the only harness.** Every fix lands
123|   behind the shared table + per-harness contract tests, and the rollout
124|   proves all six legged harnesses (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode,
125|   codex-including-its-honest-unavailable state).
126|
127|## 5. Work plan (research and big pieces first; make-change-easy before the change)
128|
129|### Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; time-boxed; no behaviour change)
130|
131|- **0.1 Muse probe parity spike.** Reproduce "new model in muse code, not
132|  in UI" end to end: run the runner leg (`discoverMuseModels`), the
133|  backend catalogue probe (`createMuseMspModelCatalog`), and the UI fetch
134|  chain against a muse CLI serving a model the caches have never seen.
135|  Measure which layer hides it (pin-wins skip, 12h cadence, 5-min MSP
136|  cache, `modelListCache` TTL, 60s client cache, `fleetLoaded` gate) and
137|  record the exact staleness budget. Output: a short findings note +
138|  failing characterization tests checked in as pending/skipped.
139|- **0.2 Autodetect matrix spike.** Build the ground-truth matrix
140|  harness × {runner autodetect, runner version probe, runner runnable
141|  loader, discovery leg, backend resolver, backend roster,
142|  UI section} for all eight ids (mock, custom, pi, muse, antigravity,
143|  vibe, opencode, codex). Confirm opencode/codex gaps and any further
144|  drift (e.g. codex transport status in `codexHarness.js`, opencode server
145|  expectations). Output: matrix doc + contract-test skeletons.

147|  central catalogue's home (extend the runner registry vs a new store),
148|  write triggers (heartbeat vs discovery event vs cadence), retention for
149|  "last seen" provenance, and the exact API shape (extend
150|  `/runners/models/catalogue`, extend `/compute/models`, or one new
151|  endpoint). Constraint: dispatch (`runnerMatches.js`,
152|  `effectiveRunnerModels`) and pickers must read the same saved list.
153|  Output: ADR-style decision record.

155|### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (seams, safety nets, no behaviour change)
156|

159|  bins, env override var, version probe bins, search-dir extras, has-leg,
160|  runnable-by-default. Rewire runner `daemon.js` tables and
161|  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` to import it. Behaviour identical;
162|  covered by the Phase 0 matrix tests.
163|- **1.2 Per-harness discovery contract tests.** For each of the six legs:
164|  canonical-key output, honest-empty classification, keep-old-slice on
165|  failure, watchdog timeout, and grammar rejection of malformed rows.
166|  Codify codex's honest-unavailable and opencode's not-configured as
167|  specified states, not gaps.
168|- **1.3 Catalogue provenance plumbing (read-only).** Add last-seen /
169|  served-by provenance to fleet catalogue entries and surface
170|  `discoveryStatus` per runner in Settings, without changing selection
171|  behaviour. This is the observability the later cutover leans on.
172|- **1.4 Alias safety net.** Characterization tests proving: unknown-model
173|  saves warn but succeed; reload never drops rows; harness switch keeps
174|  model text as a visibly-stale value. All red before Phase 3, no prod
175|  change yet.
176|
177|### Phase 2 — Fix autodetect (runner + backend agreement)
178|
179|- **2.1 Bring opencode/codex into the shared table** with correct
180|  semantics: opencode autodetects via binary *and* reachable-server
181|  signal (document which counts as "installed" vs "runnable");

186|  identically in runner logs, heartbeat `discoveryStatus`, and backend
187|  harness availability, replacing today's per-side wording.

189|  detects configured-vs-detected drift; wire it into heartbeat facts and
190|  Settings so "runner not serving an installed harness" is visible without
191|  reading logs.

193|### Phase 3 — Trusted central catalogue (the core change)
194|
195|- **3.1 Discovery-wins by default.** Flip the default so live discovery
196|  advertises and pins become explicit allowlists (`availableModels`
197|  semantics extend to the runner: pin = restrict, not freeze). Keep
198|  pin-wins as an opt-out flag for frozen fleets. Shorten/refresh cadence

98|## 4. Key decisions

100|1. **Single harness-capability table shared by runner and backend.**
101|   Autodetect bins, env overrides, version probes, discovery legs, and
102|   "runnable" status come from one module both sides import, so runner and
103|   backend can never drift again (fixes the opencode/codex gap
104|   structurally, not by adding two more entries in one file).
105|2. **Discovery-wins becomes the safe default; pins become explicit
106|   allowlists.** Keep pin-wins available as an operator opt-out, but the
107|   default advertises live discovery (freshness beats upgrade-safety once
108|   the catalogue is trusted and alias/validation paths never wipe on
109|   drift). This is the direct fix for "new model never appears".
110|3. **One central catalogue service on the backend.** It unions
111|   backend-host listings and per-runner advertised ids, normalises every
112|   option to canonical `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` via
113|   `shared/modelKeys.js`, persists the union (so UI and dispatch read the

295|  after the next automatic check, with no manual Refresh and no alias
296|  edits.
297|- Alias targets never lose their stored model to discovery drift; stale
298|  targets show a clear warning and saves always succeed.
299|- One persisted central catalogue in canonical form backs the UI pickers,
300|  alias validation, and dispatch matching.

187|  harness availability, replacing today's per-side wording.
188|- **2.3 Stale-pin hint becomes actionable.** `staleHarnessHintFor` already
189|  detects configured-vs-detected drift; wire it into heartbeat facts and
190|  Settings so "runner not serving an installed harness" is visible without
191|  reading logs.
192|
193|### Phase 3 — Trusted central catalogue (the core change)
194|
195|- **3.1 Discovery-wins by default.** Flip the default so live discovery
196|  advertises and pins become explicit allowlists (`availableModels`
197|  semantics extend to the runner: pin = restrict, not freeze). Keep
198|  pin-wins as an opt-out flag for frozen fleets. Shorten/refresh cadence
199|  so q2 ("appears at the next automatic check") holds: keep the 12h tick
200|  but add discovery on runner (re)connect, on Re-detect command, and a
201|  bounded staleness cap for the persisted list.
202|- **3.2 Central catalogue service.** Implement the Phase 0.3 design:
203|  ingest runner-advertised ids + backend-host listings, normalise to
204|  canonical keys (reject ungrammatical ids with provenance-logged drops,
205|  never silent), persist with per-option provenance, serve one endpoint
206|  the UI and dispatch share. `buildFleetModelCatalog` becomes a view over
207|  it (or is replaced by it — decided in 0.3).
208|- **3.3 UI cutover to the central list.** `useModelCatalog` reads the
209|  central endpoint; `withFleetModels` client-side merging is removed (or
210|  kept purely as a deprecated fallback for older backends during one
211|  release); `ModelSelector` and `ModelAliasesSection` render provenance
212|  ("2 runners · seen 3m ago") instead of today's dual-source badges.
213|  Refresh bypasses caches end to end (client → central service → legs).
214|- **3.4 Kill the staleness stack.** Align the four TTLs behind the central
215|  service: legs cache per-harness slices (keep), central service owns the
216|  UI-facing TTL, client keeps a short TTL only. A new CLI model must be
217|  selectable after at most one automatic check + one UI refresh, per q2.
218|
219|### Phase 4 — Alias stability (keep + warn, per q3)
220|
221|- **4.1 Never drop on write.** `normalizeModelAliases` quarantines invalid
222|  rows (kept, flagged, excluded from dispatch) instead of dropping them;
223|  projectStore surfaces the quarantine in save responses.
224|- **4.2 Never blank on drift.** `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` load path and
225|  the `ModelAliasesSection` harness switch preserve model text as a
226|  visibly-stale value; "Clear" stays an explicit user action.
227|- **4.3 Unknown harness stays hard, unknown model stays soft** —
228|  re-verify `validateAliasTargetModels` tiers after the catalogue move so
229|  a central-catalogue outage can never block alias saves (probe-null ⇒
230|  warn nothing, as today).
231|
232|### Phase 5 — Assurance and rollout
233|
234|- **5.1 Test gates.** `npm run test:unit` green; new suites: shared-table
235|  parity (runner vs backend resolve identically on fixtures), leg
236|  contracts, central-catalogue golden tests (ingest → normalise → persist
237|  → serve), alias no-data-loss tests, UI picker tests against the central
238|  endpoint (existing `useModelCatalog` / `ModelSelector` /
239|  `ModelAliasesSection` suites updated, not deleted). Headless checks via
240|  existing mock fixtures or `npm run capture:screenshot`; no long-lived
241|  background servers.
242|- **5.2 Docs.** Update runner docs (autodetect + discovery-wins +
243|  Re-detect), Settings help text, the model-key grammar doc if "effort"
244|  wording appears anywhere (rename to reasoning level), and the ADR from
245|  0.3. Add an operator runbook: "new model not appearing" (check
246|  discoveryStatus → Re-detect → staleness cap) and "alias target stale"
247|  (warning meaning + fix path).
248|- **5.3 Rollout.** Ship Phase 1 behind no flags (refactor only); Phase 2
249|  with per-harness logging; Phase 3 behind a single
250|  `centralCatalog` flag with dual-read comparison logging (central vs
251|  legacy merge) for one release before cutover; Phase 4 with quarantine
252|  metrics. Rollback = flag off + pin-wins opt-out documented.
253|
254|## 6. Validation plan (per phase)
255|
256|- 0.1: reproduction script shows the new-model journey across every layer
257|  with timestamps; characterization tests fail for the right reason.
258|- 0.2: matrix has zero "unknown" cells; every cell links to code or a
259|  contract test.
260|- 0.3: ADR signed off; dispatch and UI proven to read the same store in a
261|  spike test.
262|- 1.1–1.4: `npm run test:unit` green with zero behaviour diff (dual-run
263|  old vs new tables on fixtures).
264|- 2.x: fixture-host tests prove opencode/codex detect/no-detect correctly
265|  on both sides; stale-pin hint visible in heartbeat facts fixture.
266|- 3.x: golden test — runner advertises `muse::meta::<new>` → central list
267|  contains it with provenance → picker offers it → dispatch matches it
268|  verbatim; staleness test — new model selectable within one check cycle.
269|- 4.x: no-data-loss tests — drifted/invalid/stale alias rows survive
270|  save → reload → save with warnings and zero silent mutation.
271|- 5.x: full `npm run test:unit`, lint, docs link check
272|  (`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` path per repo convention), screenshot
273|  smoke of picker + aliases pages.
274|
275|## 7. Risks and open questions
276|
277|- The survey was never answered; q1–q4 assumptions need owner confirmation
278|  before Phase 3 (wrong q2/q4 changes the catalogue design).
279|- Codex live transport is unverified — 2.1 must not promise codex
280|  discovery, only honest codex detectability.
281|- Opencode "installed" definition (binary present vs server reachable) is
282|  genuinely ambiguous — 0.2/2.1 decides, both states stay expressible.
283|- Behaviour risk: flipping to discovery-wins changes what pinned fleets
284|  advertise — mitigated by the opt-out flag, dual-read logging, and the
285|  quarantine path in 4.1.
286|- Non-goals: new harness additions beyond the eight known ids; changing
287|  the `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` grammar; dispatch matching
288|  semantics beyond reading the shared list; UI redesign of the pickers.
289|
290|## 8. Success criteria
291|
292|- Every legged harness autodetects identically on runner and backend, with
293|  contract tests pinning the agreement.
294|- A model released in any attached harness CLI is selectable in the UI
295|  after the next automatic check, with no manual Refresh and no alias
296|  edits.
297|- Alias targets never lose their stored model to discovery drift; stale
298|  targets show a clear warning and saves always succeed.
299|- One persisted central catalogue in canonical form backs the UI pickers,
300|  alias validation, and dispatch matching.

# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Runner autodetect + trusted model catalogue + alias stability

Task: `9be2458f-c691-4772-90e7-eef1cc2f27c4` — "Runners are not autodetecting correctly".
Stage: plan only. No code changes in this stage.

## 1. Goal

Fix runner autodetect (muse known-broken, others suspected), stop muse alias
targets losing their stored model, and build one firm, trusted model
catalogue: model options flow from each runner's harness discovery into the
kainbain-standard `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` form, are saved
centrally, and the UI selects from that central list.

## 2. Starting evidence (what the codebase shows today)

All paths verified by reading the code this session. No prior report was
taken on trust.

- Runner discovery legs live in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`
  (`DISCOVERY_LEGS`: pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode, codex). Each leg
  reuses its backend harness's own `listModels()` surface, runs behind a
  20s watchdog (`DISCOVER_LEG_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS`), and keeps the previous
  per-harness slice on failure.
- The daemon (`runner/daemon.js`) seeds `discoveredModelsCache` at boot and
  refreshes on `modelDiscoveryIntervalMs` (default 12h,
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js`). Heartbeats advertise
  `models: resolveAdvertisedModels(config, discovered)` — **pin-wins by
  default**: when `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`MODEL` is set,
  `refreshDiscoveredModels` skips scanning entirely unless
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`. A pinned runner can therefore
  never surface a newly released model.
- Runner harness autodetect (`detectAvailableHarnesses`,
  `AUTO_DETECTABLE_HARNESSES = ["pi","muse","antigravity","vibe"]`,
  `HARNESS_DETECT_BINS`, `defaultLoadHarness`) knows only five harnesses.
  **opencode and codex have discovery legs but are absent from runner
  autodetect, version probing, and the runnable-harness loader** — the
  backend resolver (`api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js`) does cover
  codex/opencode (`KAINBAIN_CODEX_BIN`, `KAINBAIN_OPENCODE_BIN`,
  `~/.opencode/bin`). The two sides have drifted.
- Leg asymmetry: codex always throws `CODEX_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` (live
  transport unverified); opencode requires an `OPENCODE_URL` server on the
  runner host (`OPENCODE_NOT_CONFIGURED` otherwise); muse spawns
  `muse serve` stdio `model/list` and throws `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` on a
  zero-row answer.
- The fleet catalogue (`api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.js`,
  `buildFleetModelCatalog`) is derived **live** from claim-eligible runner
  registrations, served at `GET /runners/models/catalogue`, and gated by
  `effectiveRunnerModels` (operator `availableModels` allowlist wins over
  advertised). It is never cached — good — but it is a *second* catalogue,
  not the one the pickers primarily read.
- The pickers primarily read `GET /compute/models` (backend-host catalogue
  via `aggregateModelCatalog` in `api/models.js`, per-harness honest lists,
  curated fallback for the default harness only), fetched once on mount by
  `useModelCatalog` (`frontend/src/hooks/useModelCatalog.js`) with a 60s
  client cache, on top of backend TTLs (shared `modelListCache`, 5-min muse
  MSP cache in `api/agent/harnesses/muse/msp/museMspModelCatalog.js`,
  per-harness timeout in `api/crew/modelDiscovery.js`). Fleet ids are merged
  in client-side by `withFleetModels`/`fleetModelsForHarness`
  (`frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/`) as exact advertised ids with
  strict harness attribution, gated on `fleetLoaded`. So today there are
  **two sources merged in the browser**, with at least four TTLs between a
  new CLI model and a visible option. That explains "new muse model visible
  in muse code but not in the UI".
- "Effort" in the task text does not exist as a catalogue segment. The real
  grammar (`shared/modelKeys.js`) is
  `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]`; runner `tiers` (`T0,T1`,
  `runner/config.js`, dispatch gate `TIER_CEILING`) are a separate fleet
  concept. The plan treats "effort" = reasoning level and keeps tiers
  distinct (see survey assumption q4).
- Alias wipe paths found: (a) `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` harness `onChange`
  always writes `{ harness: next, model: "" }`; (b) `normalizeModelAliases`
  (`shared/modelAliases.js`) **drops** grammar-invalid rows on every
  projectStore write path (`api/projectStore.js`); (c)
  `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` (`api/aliasTargets.js`) blanks models on
  `none`-harness targets at load; (d) save-time hard errors refuse unknown
  harness / `none`+model / malformed ref / unadvertised reasoning level
  (`validateAliasTargetModels`). Catalogue-miss is already soft (warning
  only) — that part matches the desired behaviour and must be preserved.
- Survey state: `SURVEY.md` exists in this task folder but `answers` is
  empty (unanswered), and the referenced `idea-20261110-212333.md` is not
  present in the folder. The plan adopts the survey's Recommended options
  as assumptions (Section 3) and flags them for confirmation.

## 3. Survey assumptions (Recommended options adopted, unconfirmed)

- q1 — scope: **all connected tools, fixed properly** (not muse-only).
- q2 — new-model arrival: **appears on its own at the next automatic
  check** (no manual Refresh required, though Refresh stays as an escape
  hatch).
- q3 — alias target stops being detected: **keep the saved value and show
  a clear warning** (never auto-retarget, never blank, never block saves).
- q4 — "effort" segment: **thinking depth / reasoning level** (the existing
  4th `::reasoning` segment), not speed/quality tier. Tiers stay a separate
  dispatch concept.

If any assumption is wrong, Phase 0 re-plans before code changes.

## 4. Key decisions

1. **Single harness-capability table shared by runner and backend.**
   Autodetect bins, env overrides, version probes, discovery legs, and
   "runnable" status come from one module both sides import, so runner and
   backend can never drift again (fixes the opencode/codex gap
   structurally, not by adding two more entries in one file).
2. **Discovery-wins becomes the safe default; pins become explicit
   allowlists.** Keep pin-wins available as an operator opt-out, but the
   default advertises live discovery (freshness beats upgrade-safety once
   the catalogue is trusted and alias/validation paths never wipe on
   drift). This is the direct fix for "new model never appears".
3. **One central catalogue service on the backend.** It unions
   backend-host listings and per-runner advertised ids, normalises every
   option to canonical `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` via
   `shared/modelKeys.js`, persists the union (so UI and dispatch read the
   same saved list), and records provenance per option (which runner(s) /
   backend host serve it, when last seen). The UI selects from this list;
   the fleet merge moves server-side and the browser stops merging two
   sources.
4. **Aliases never lose data to discovery drift.** Catalogue-miss stays
   soft everywhere; invalid rows are quarantined with a warning instead of
   dropped; harness switches preserve the model text until the user picks a
   replacement.
5. **Muse is the pilot harness, not the only harness.** Every fix lands
   behind the shared table + per-harness contract tests, and the rollout
   proves all six legged harnesses (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode,
   codex-including-its-honest-unavailable state).

## 5. Work plan (research and big pieces first; make-change-easy before the change)

### Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; time-boxed; no behaviour change)

- **0.1 Muse probe parity spike.** Reproduce "new model in muse code, not
  in UI" end to end: run the runner leg (`discoverMuseModels`), the
  backend catalogue probe (`createMuseMspModelCatalog`), and the UI fetch
  chain against a muse CLI serving a model the caches have never seen.
  Measure which layer hides it (pin-wins skip, 12h cadence, 5-min MSP
  cache, `modelListCache` TTL, 60s client cache, `fleetLoaded` gate) and
  record the exact staleness budget. Output: a short findings note +
  failing characterization tests checked in as pending/skipped.
- **0.2 Autodetect matrix spike.** Build the ground-truth matrix
  harness × {runner autodetect, runner version probe, runner runnable
  loader, discovery leg, backend resolver, backend roster,
  UI section} for all eight ids (mock, custom, pi, muse, antigravity,
  vibe, opencode, codex). Confirm opencode/codex gaps and any further
  drift (e.g. codex transport status in `codexHarness.js`, opencode server
  expectations). Output: matrix doc + contract-test skeletons.
- **0.3 Catalogue consolidation design spike.** Decide the persisted
  central catalogue's home (extend the runner registry vs a new store),
  write triggers (heartbeat vs discovery event vs cadence), retention for
  "last seen" provenance, and the exact API shape (extend
  `/runners/models/catalogue`, extend `/compute/models`, or one new
  endpoint). Constraint: dispatch (`runnerMatches.js`,
  `effectiveRunnerModels`) and pickers must read the same saved list.
  Output: ADR-style decision record.

### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (seams, safety nets, no behaviour change)

- **1.1 Extract the shared harness-capability table.** New dependency-free
  module (next to `shared/modelKeys.js`) owning per-harness: autodetect
  bins, env override var, version probe bins, search-dir extras, has-leg,
  runnable-by-default. Rewire runner `daemon.js` tables and
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` to import it. Behaviour identical;
  covered by the Phase 0 matrix tests.
- **1.2 Per-harness discovery contract tests.** For each of the six legs:
  canonical-key output, honest-empty classification, keep-old-slice on
  failure, watchdog timeout, and grammar rejection of malformed rows.
  Codify codex's honest-unavailable and opencode's not-configured as
  specified states, not gaps.
- **1.3 Catalogue provenance plumbing (read-only).** Add last-seen /
  served-by provenance to fleet catalogue entries and surface
  `discoveryStatus` per runner in Settings, without changing selection
  behaviour. This is the observability the later cutover leans on.
- **1.4 Alias safety net.** Characterization tests proving: unknown-model
  saves warn but succeed; reload never drops rows; harness switch keeps
  model text as a visibly-stale value. All red before Phase 3, no prod
  change yet.

### Phase 2 — Fix autodetect (runner + backend agreement)

- **2.1 Bring opencode/codex into the shared table** with correct
  semantics: opencode autodetects via binary *and* reachable-server
  signal (document which counts as "installed" vs "runnable");
  codex autodetects via binary + auth store
  (`codexAuthPath`) while discovery stays honestly unavailable until the
  transport lands.
- **2.2 Single "installed / runnable / discoverable" vocabulary** surfaced
  identically in runner logs, heartbeat `discoveryStatus`, and backend
  harness availability, replacing today's per-side wording.
- **2.3 Stale-pin hint becomes actionable.** `staleHarnessHintFor` already
  detects configured-vs-detected drift; wire it into heartbeat facts and
  Settings so "runner not serving an installed harness" is visible without
  reading logs.

### Phase 3 — Trusted central catalogue (the core change)

- **3.1 Discovery-wins by default.** Flip the default so live discovery
  advertises and pins become explicit allowlists (`availableModels`
  semantics extend to the runner: pin = restrict, not freeze). Keep
  pin-wins as an opt-out flag for frozen fleets. Shorten/refresh cadence
  so q2 ("appears at the next automatic check") holds: keep the 12h tick
  but add discovery on runner (re)connect, on Re-detect command, and a
  bounded staleness cap for the persisted list.
- **3.2 Central catalogue service.** Implement the Phase 0.3 design:
  ingest runner-advertised ids + backend-host listings, normalise to
  canonical keys (reject ungrammatical ids with provenance-logged drops,
  never silent), persist with per-option provenance, serve one endpoint
  the UI and dispatch share. `buildFleetModelCatalog` becomes a view over
  it (or is replaced by it — decided in 0.3).
- **3.3 UI cutover to the central list.** `useModelCatalog` reads the
  central endpoint; `withFleetModels` client-side merging is removed (or
  kept purely as a deprecated fallback for older backends during one
  release); `ModelSelector` and `ModelAliasesSection` render provenance
  ("2 runners · seen 3m ago") instead of today's dual-source badges.
  Refresh bypasses caches end to end (client → central service → legs).
- **3.4 Kill the staleness stack.** Align the four TTLs behind the central
  service: legs cache per-harness slices (keep), central service owns the
  UI-facing TTL, client keeps a short TTL only. A new CLI model must be
  selectable after at most one automatic check + one UI refresh, per q2.

### Phase 4 — Alias stability (keep + warn, per q3)

- **4.1 Never drop on write.** `normalizeModelAliases` quarantines invalid
  rows (kept, flagged, excluded from dispatch) instead of dropping them;
  projectStore surfaces the quarantine in save responses.
- **4.2 Never blank on drift.** `sanitizeAliasTargetModels` load path and
  the `ModelAliasesSection` harness switch preserve model text as a
  visibly-stale value; "Clear" stays an explicit user action.
- **4.3 Unknown harness stays hard, unknown model stays soft** —
  re-verify `validateAliasTargetModels` tiers after the catalogue move so
  a central-catalogue outage can never block alias saves (probe-null ⇒
  warn nothing, as today).

### Phase 5 — Assurance and rollout

- **5.1 Test gates.** `npm run test:unit` green; new suites: shared-table
  parity (runner vs backend resolve identically on fixtures), leg
  contracts, central-catalogue golden tests (ingest → normalise → persist
  → serve), alias no-data-loss tests, UI picker tests against the central
  endpoint (existing `useModelCatalog` / `ModelSelector` /
  `ModelAliasesSection` suites updated, not deleted). Headless checks via
  existing mock fixtures or `npm run capture:screenshot`; no long-lived
  background servers.
- **5.2 Docs.** Update runner docs (autodetect + discovery-wins +
  Re-detect), Settings help text, the model-key grammar doc if "effort"
  wording appears anywhere (rename to reasoning level), and the ADR from
  0.3. Add an operator runbook: "new model not appearing" (check
  discoveryStatus → Re-detect → staleness cap) and "alias target stale"
  (warning meaning + fix path).
- **5.3 Rollout.** Ship Phase 1 behind no flags (refactor only); Phase 2
  with per-harness logging; Phase 3 behind a single
  `centralCatalog` flag with dual-read comparison logging (central vs
  legacy merge) for one release before cutover; Phase 4 with quarantine
  metrics. Rollback = flag off + pin-wins opt-out documented.

## 6. Validation plan (per phase)

- 0.1: reproduction script shows the new-model journey across every layer
  with timestamps; characterization tests fail for the right reason.
- 0.2: matrix has zero "unknown" cells; every cell links to code or a
  contract test.
- 0.3: ADR signed off; dispatch and UI proven to read the same store in a
  spike test.
- 1.1–1.4: `npm run test:unit` green with zero behaviour diff (dual-run
  old vs new tables on fixtures).
- 2.x: fixture-host tests prove opencode/codex detect/no-detect correctly
  on both sides; stale-pin hint visible in heartbeat facts fixture.
- 3.x: golden test — runner advertises `muse::meta::<new>` → central list
  contains it with provenance → picker offers it → dispatch matches it
  verbatim; staleness test — new model selectable within one check cycle.
- 4.x: no-data-loss tests — drifted/invalid/stale alias rows survive
  save → reload → save with warnings and zero silent mutation.
- 5.x: full `npm run test:unit`, lint, docs link check
  (`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` path per repo convention), screenshot
  smoke of picker + aliases pages.

## 7. Risks and open questions

- The survey was never answered; q1–q4 assumptions need owner confirmation
  before Phase 3 (wrong q2/q4 changes the catalogue design).
- Codex live transport is unverified — 2.1 must not promise codex
  discovery, only honest codex detectability.
- Opencode "installed" definition (binary present vs server reachable) is
  genuinely ambiguous — 0.2/2.1 decides, both states stay expressible.
- Behaviour risk: flipping to discovery-wins changes what pinned fleets
  advertise — mitigated by the opt-out flag, dual-read logging, and the
  quarantine path in 4.1.
- Non-goals: new harness additions beyond the eight known ids; changing
  the `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` grammar; dispatch matching
  semantics beyond reading the shared list; UI redesign of the pickers.

## 8. Success criteria

- Every legged harness autodetects identically on runner and backend, with
  contract tests pinning the agreement.
- A model released in any attached harness CLI is selectable in the UI
  after the next automatic check, with no manual Refresh and no alias
  edits.
- Alias targets never lose their stored model to discovery drift; stale
  targets show a clear warning and saves always succeed.
- One persisted central catalogue in canonical form backs the UI pickers,
  alias validation, and dispatch matching.

  `effectiveRunnerModels`) and pickers must read the same saved list.

  canonical-key output, honest-empty classification, keep-old-slice on
  failure, watchdog timeout, and grammar rejection of malformed rows.
  Codify codex's honest-unavailable and opencode's not-configured as
  specified states, not gaps.
- **1.3 Catalogue provenance plumbing (read-only).** Add last-seen /
  served-by provenance to fleet catalogue entries and surface

  reading logs.

  advertises and pins become explicit allowlists (`availableModels`
  semantics extend to the runner: pin = restrict, not freeze). Keep

# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Runner autodetect + trusted model catalogue + alias stability

Task: `9be2458f-c691-4772-90e7-eef1cc2f27c4` — "Runners are not autodetecting correctly".
Stage: plan only. No code changes in this stage.

## 1. Goal

Fix runner autodetect (muse known-broken, others suspected), stop muse alias
targets losing their stored model, and build one firm, trusted model
catalogue: model options flow from each runner's harness discovery into the
kainbain-standard `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]` form, are saved
centrally, and the UI selects from that central list.

## 2. Starting evidence (what the codebase shows today)

All paths verified by reading the code this session. No prior report was
taken on trust.

- Runner discovery legs live in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`
  (`DISCOVERY_LEGS`: pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, opencode, codex). Each leg
  reuses its backend harness's own `listModels()` surface, runs behind a
  20s watchdog (`DISCOVER_LEG_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS`), and keeps the previous
  per-harness slice on failure.
- The daemon (`runner/daemon.js`) seeds `discoveredModelsCache` at boot and
  refreshes on `modelDiscoveryIntervalMs` (default 12h,
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js`). Heartbeats advertise
  `models: resolveAdvertisedModels(config, discovered)` — **pin-wins by
  default**: when `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`MODEL` is set,
  `refreshDiscoveredModels` skips scanning entirely unless
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`. A pinned runner can therefore
  never surface a newly released model.
- Runner harness autodetect (`detectAvailableHarnesses`,
  `AUTO_DETECTABLE_HARNESSES = ["pi","muse","antigravity","vibe"]`,
  `HARNESS_DETECT_BINS`, `defaultLoadHarness`) knows only five harnesses.
  **opencode and codex have discovery legs but are absent from runner
  autodetect, version probing, and the runnable-harness loader** — the
  backend resolver (`api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js`) does cover
  codex/opencode (`KAINBAIN_CODEX_BIN`, `KAINBAIN_OPENCODE_BIN`,
  `~/.opencode/bin`). The two sides have drifted.
- Leg asymmetry: codex always throws `CODEX_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` (live
  transport unverified); opencode requires an `OPENCODE_URL` server on the
  runner host (`OPENCODE_NOT_CONFIGURED` otherwise); muse spawns
  `muse serve` stdio `model/list` and throws `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` on a
  zero-row answer.
- The fleet catalogue (`api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.js`,
  `buildFleetModelCatalog`) is derived **live** from claim-eligible runner
  registrations, served at `GET /runners/models/catalogue`, and gated by
  `effectiveRunnerModels` (operator `availableModels` allowlist wins over
  advertised). It is never cached — good — but it is a *second* catalogue,
  not the one the pickers primarily read.

  via `aggregateModelCatalog` in `api/models.js`, per-harness honest lists,
  curated fallback for the default harness only), fetched once on mount by
  `useModelCatalog` (`frontend/src/hooks/useModelCatalog.js`) with a 60s
  client cache, on top of backend TTLs (shared `modelListCache`, 5-min muse
  MSP cache in `api/agent/harnesses/muse/msp/museMspModelCatalog.js`,
  per-harness timeout in `api/crew/modelDiscovery.js`). Fleet ids are merged
  in client-side by `withFleetModels`/`fleetModelsForHarness`

  strict harness attribution, gated on `fleetLoaded`. So today there are
  **two sources merged in the browser**, with at least four TTLs between a
  new CLI model and a visible option. That explains "new muse model visible
  in muse code but not in the UI".

  grammar (`shared/modelKeys.js`) is
  `harness::provider::id[::reasoning]`; runner `tiers` (`T0,T1`,
  `runner/config.js`, dispatch gate `TIER_CEILING`) are a separate fleet
  concept. The plan treats "effort" = reasoning level and keeps tiers
  distinct (see survey assumption q4).
